artworks.title: Paris and Oenone
artworks.description: Lastman's pastoral stages the Idaean shepherd Paris with the nymph Oenone — the first love he abandons for Helen, whose later refusal to heal his wound seals Troy's fall. Rembrandt's teacher makes the Cebrenid nymph the quiet counterpoint to the Judgment of Paris.

artworks.title: Paris and Oenone
artworks.description: Blommendael's Dutch canvas returns to the lovers on Mount Ida: Paris crowned with flowers, Oenone the river-nymph who will outlive his betrayal. Baroque pastoral keeps her as the abandoned healer of the Trojan cycle.

artworks.title: Oenone
artworks.description: Britten's plate for Tennyson's early poems illustrates the monologue 'Oenone' — the nymph alone on Ida after Paris leaves for Helen. Victorian book art made her grief the English face of the Trojan prelude.

artworks.title: Paris and Oenone (House of the Labyrinth, Pompeii)
artworks.description: Fresco remains from Pompeii's House of the Labyrinth preserve Paris with Oenone in a Roman domestic cycle — the Idaean couple painted for a Campanian villa long before Helen's name eclipsed hers.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix Trojan War series restores Oenone to the screen as Paris' first love on Ida — the nymph the epic cycle remembers when the arrows of Philoctetes finally find him.

popCulture.title: Heroides
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Heroides 5 is Oenone's letter to Paris — the abandoned nymph's voice that became the defining literary reception of the Cebrenid, read beside Helen's later fame.

popCulture.title: Oenone
popCulture.creator: Alfred, Lord Tennyson
popCulture.description: Tennyson's dramatic monologue gives the Idaean nymph the English Romantic stage: Oenone alone after the Judgment, waiting for a Paris who will not return.
